paper_id: Boosting DNN Cold Inference on Edge Devices
title: Boosting DNN Cold Inference on Devices
motivation: DNN inference on edge devices often occurs in cold manner (1.5×-443.5× slower than warm), hurting user experience for apps like PDF scanners and beauty cameras
problem_framing: Optimize three tightly coupled stages: weights reading, weights transformation, and model execution across asymmetric edge processors
key_insight: Kernel selected by warm inference speed is suboptimal for cold inference; Winograd kernels execute fast but incur heavy transformation cost that dominates cold latency
method_signature: Heuristic kernel scheduler balancing operation-to-processor affinity and pipeline overlapping across big.LITTLE cores
evaluation_criteria: Cold inference latency reduction vs TFLite/ncnn/AsyMo on Meizu 16T CPU and Jetson TX2 GPU; ablation of each optimization knob
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Problem is NP-hard, cannot obtain optimal kernel scheduling plan directly; multithreading weights read/transformation has limited benefit
evidence_for_taste: fastest kernel in warm inference does not necessarily best in cold
weight sharing approaches are not scalable
we do not need to iterate over all combinations
thinking_moves: 从工程异常反推设计空间失效: 现有DNN引擎的kernel选择策略只考虑warm inference速度
识别出三个耦合的优化维度需联合考虑
利用DNN的layer-by-layer结构特征构建流水线并行机会
识别操作与硬件的亲和性差异(执行对大核敏感, I/O对资源争用敏感)
